findings.claim: The repository pin is trust-on-first-use and is written implicitly by whichever gh-using verb first runs (integrate, record-landing, the reviewer's server compare). If the remote or gh default is already repointed when that first call happens, the attacker's repository becomes the pinned one and every later check trusts it. The docs call it trust-on-first-use, but nothing makes the operator set the pin deliberately.
findings.evidence: if (!pinned) await writeJson(path, { repo_id, nameWithOwner: repo, ... }) runs inside pinnedGithubRepo, which githubCompare, serverLeadAutonomy and integrateViaPullRequest each call on demand. No operator step or admission step seeds the pin.
findings.fix: Seed the pin from an operator-only step (for example ao-topology permissions install, or lead ensure run from an operator shell), and have pinnedGithubRepo refuse rather than create when no pin exists in a managed session. Or at minimum have the first pin write show up in manage status or doctor so the operator notices it.

findings.claim: All three findings from 32b49d7 are resolved. (1) The dist diff is now limited to this task's source (pinnedGithubRepo, githubCompare and a fingerprint change) after rebasing onto TM-264's rebuild. (2) The GitHub repository is pinned in host state, and every later gh call names it (--repo on pr list, checks, merge and view, and the name in the api path). A disagreeing resolution refuses integrate as repository, drops lead autonomy to grant-required, and fails the server compare, with tests (i) covering it. (3) record-landing by the locally found lead is refused when the server lead_autonomy policy names a different lead, with test (j). The no-policy local-trust bound is documented. The TM-263 acceptance criteria are otherwise met as in the prior review: grantless record-landing is gated on the server default branch and the approved revision, the policy is read only from the server, unavailability fails closed, workers and non-leads are refused, the config sets integrate_via and lead_autonomy, and the docs cover revocation and what is no longer protected. The request includes no test or build output.
